column4: This ayah states the section's whole three-part architecture at once: earth is a settled floor, heaven is بِنَاءً, and God fashions human forms beautifully.
Earth as فِرَاشًا and heaven as بِنَاءً are the section's floor and roof in the Quran's own explicit domestic wording.
Creation of the heavens and earth is immediately joined to God's fashioning human beings well, supporting the section's move from the cosmic house to its human structure.
The challenge to human beings asks whether they or heaven are harder to create and answers بَنَاهَا, explicitly comparing the human structure with the built sky.
Within the construction begun at 79:27, God raises the sky's thickness and فَسَوَّاهَا; the same finishing verb that the section applies to the soul finishes the roof.
After the roof of 79:27-28, earth is دَحَاهَا; the source section explicitly identifies dahw as the parallel of its tahw, so this completes the same roof-and-floor sequence.
وَالسَّمَاءَ بَنَيْنَاهَا presents God directly as the powerful builder of the section's upper structure.
Beside the built heaven of 51:47, وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَاهَا makes earth the spread furnishing beneath it.
The sky is بَنَيْنَاهَا, adorned, and without fissures, giving the section's roof both construction and finished integrity.
The earth is extended immediately after the intact built sky of 50:6, completing that passage's floor beneath the roof.
سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا names heaven itself as a protected roof, the section's central architectural identification.
The oath by السَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ names the sky as the raised ceiling over the cosmic house.
وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا depicts the heavens as seven strong structures built directly above the occupants.
Calling earth مِهَادًا gives the cosmic house its prepared lower bedding.
Mountains as أَوْتَادًا supply the pegs beside the earth-bedding of 78:6, making the section's tent reading concrete.
وَزَرَابِيُّ مَبْثُوثَةٌ supplies literal spread carpets just before 88:18-20 asks the reader to see the raised sky and spread earth.
The question كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ directs sight to heaven as an elevated overhead structure.
The question كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ presents earth as a laid-out surface beneath the raised sky of 88:18.
God raises heaven and places the balance; the ayah brings the elevated roof and measured order together just as the section joins sky and a balanced soul.
وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ lays earth down for its inhabitants beneath the raised heaven of 55:7.
After creating what is on earth, God turns to heaven and فَسَوَّاهُنَّ as seven heavens, joining the lower realm to a divinely finished upper structure.
God raises the heavens بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا; the roof is explicitly architectural while its lack of visible pillars marks a boundary with the section's tent-poles and bodily ribs.
Heaven is created without visible pillars and mountains are cast into earth to steady it, pairing a supportless roof with a stabilized floor.
Earth is مَدَدْنَاهَا and its growth is مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَوْزُونٍ; the spread floor and measured fitness appear in one scene.
وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الْأَرْضَ directly restages the section's act of spreading the lower surface.
God makes earth مَهْدًا for the addressees, presenting the ground as an inhabitable bedding.
Earth is made مَهْدًا and furnished with ways, so the section's floor is shown as fitted for those living on it.
وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ بِسَاطًا explicitly calls earth a carpet spread for human beings.
Houses from animal hides and furnishings from wool, camel hair, and hair are the Quranic realization of the section's leather tent and wool-or-camel-hair floor covering.
God makes ظِلَالًا from created things immediately after the hide-tents of 16:80, realizing the section's definition of an overhead structure by the shade it gives.
خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ addresses the human directly as created, finished, and balanced, exactly the section's reading of the soul's سَوَّاهَا.
فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَا شَاءَ رَكَّبَكَ completes 82:7 by describing the human as assembled into a chosen form, matching building as joining parts.
ثُمَّ سَوَّاهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِهِ joins divine fashioning to the breath that makes the body live, matching the section's definition of nafs as its living spirit.
God's command follows فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ with breathing into the human from His spirit, directly coupling the finished structure with life.
The repeated Adam scene again places divine breathing after سَوَّيْتُهُ, confirming the section's link between a formed body and its living inward principle.
لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ states the human result as the finest formed constitution, parallel to the section's flawless sawiyy form.
The source dictionary explicitly glosses sound binya as fiṭra; فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا names that God-given native constitution.
From the clot introduced by 75:37, فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى makes human creation culminate in the same act of proportioning used for the section's soul.
الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى makes creation followed by fitting completion a general signature of the Lord praised here.
مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ presents the human as created and precisely apportioned, clarifying the measured fitness implied by the section's balancing.
Bones are made and clothed with flesh before أَنْشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ; this staged assembly makes the living human a structure whose parts precede a further creation.
مُخَلَّقَةٍ وَغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ distinguishes formed from unformed embryonic substance and traces it to mature human life, exposing the process behind the finished structure.
نَحْنُ خَلَقْنَاهُمْ وَشَدَدْنَا أَسْرَهُمْ describes God creating people and strengthening their bodily bonds or frame, close to the section's parts joined into a sound build.
Creation from نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ leads to human creation stage after stage within three darknesses, joining the living self to a nested work of construction.
God takes الْأَنْفُسَ at death and in sleep, retaining some and returning others; this directly tests the section's dictionary definition of nafs by bodily life and its cessation.
Human creation and resurrection are كَنَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ, making the single nafs the measure of how effortlessly the Builder can form all people.
The creation of heavens and earth is declared greater than creating humankind, directly comparing the cosmic structure with the human one as 79:27 does.
The Creator of the heavens and earth is asked whether He can create the like of human beings, making cosmic building evidence for rebuilding the person.
Creation of the heavens and earth is the stated proof that God can create human beings again, joining the outer house to the maker of its mortal occupants.
The One who created the heavens and earth without fatigue is declared able to revive the dead, so cosmic construction warrants restoration of the living structure.
The seven layered heavens show no disparity in the Merciful's creation, echoing the section's completed, flaw-free form and 50:6's unbroken roof.
Repeated sight returns unable to find a flaw in the heavens of 67:3, making the roof's finished integrity an examined fact rather than a bare assertion.
God completes the seven heavens, assigns each its order, adorns the nearest with lamps, and protects it; construction, fitting, decoration, and guarding coincide.
The nearest heaven is adorned with lamps that also serve against devils, combining the roof's beauty with active protection.
إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا adorns the nearest heaven with stars, matching the section's built and decorated ceiling.
وَحِفْظًا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ مَارِدٍ adds guarding to the adorned heaven of 37:6, spelling out its protected-roof function.
Constellations are placed in heaven and it is beautified for viewers, another direct depiction of the roof as intentionally finished and adorned.
وَحَفِظْنَاهَا follows the adorned heaven of 15:16 with protection from every expelled devil.
God holds heaven back from falling on earth except by His leave, dramatizing how the overhead roof is sustained above the floor.
Heaven and earth stand by God's command, and the same voice will call human beings out from earth, joining the house's stability to its occupants' renewed life.
أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ وَاسْتَعْمَرَكُمْ فِيهَا makes humans from the house's floor and appoints them to inhabit and cultivate it.
The mountain is raised above the people كَأَنَّهُ ظُلَّةٌ and they fear it will fall; an overhead canopy becomes a threatening reversal of the protective, shading roof.
The three-branched shade introduced at 77:30 is لَا ظَلِيلٍ وَلَا يُغْنِي مِنَ اللَّهَبِ, explicitly denying both shade and protection that define the section's canopy.
عَذَابُ يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ turns the very image of a shade-canopy into the setting of punishment rather than shelter.
Heaven splits and becomes وَاهِيَةٌ on that day, the direct future reversal of the intact, protected ceiling in the section.
God will roll heaven like a written scroll and repeat creation as He began it, setting the roof's dismantling beside the Builder's power to rebuild.
The day earth is replaced by another earth and the heavens as well marks the temporal boundary of the present floor-and-roof arrangement.
The heavens will be folded in God's right hand, reversing the section's image of the presently extended overhead structure.
وَإِذَا السَّمَاءُ كُشِطَتْ pictures the sky stripped away, exposing the eventual removal of the cosmic canopy.
إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْفَطَرَتْ directly reverses the roof with no fissures by showing it split open at the final event.
إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْشَقَّتْ places the obedient sky's splitting at the end of its present architectural order.
وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ repeats the act of extending earth in an eschatological setting, turning the created floor into the surface prepared for final disclosure.
السَّمَاءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ makes the promised Day capable of rending the roof, a boundary to its present protection.
The raised heaven of 55:7 will later split and change appearance, marking the end of the balanced structure described earlier in the same surah.
وَإِذَا السَّمَاءُ فُرِجَتْ opens the sky, reversing the no-fissure ceiling of 50:6.
The heaven that 78:12 calls a strong built structure will be opened into gates, an internal reversal in the same surah.
The day heaven splits with cloud and angels descend turns the overhead expanse into an opened boundary rather than a closed roof.
In the surah that swears by the raised roof at 52:5, heaven will later sway violently, exposing the constructed order's final limit.
دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا دَكًّا crushes the spread floor flat at judgment, reversing its present settled use.
Earth and mountains are lifted and crushed in one blow, dismantling both the floor and its peg-like fixtures.
Mountains are set upright between the raised sky of 88:18 and spread earth of 88:20; read with 78:7, they function as the scene's structural pegs.
God makes good everything He creates and begins human creation from clay, supplying the rule of workmanship behind the fashioned, ensouled human of 32:9.
The human line is made from an extract of fluid before the fashioning and breath of 32:9, contributing the material stage of the third structure.
The human begins as an emitted drop and then a clot, providing the material sequence that 75:38 completes with خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى.
After the fashioning of 75:38, God makes the human pair male and female, showing one consequence of that fitted form.
Human creation begins from an extract of clay, the first material step in the assembled bodily scene completed at 23:14.
The drop is placed in قَرَارٍ مَكِينٍ, a secure lodging that immediately precedes the successive construction of 23:14.
The ayah traces human beings through dust, drop, clot, childhood, strength, age, and death, showing the built self as a staged and time-bounded formation.
Humanity is made from نُطْفَةٍ أَمْشَاجٍ, a mixed drop, and furnished with hearing and sight, a concrete joining and fitting of capacities.
The command that the human look at what he was created from frames 86:6-7 as an inspection of the bodily structure's origin.
Creation from an ejected fluid supplies the living body's generative material before 86:7 locates its emergence within the torso.

The fluid emerges from between the backbone and التَّرَائِبِ, the chest or breastbones, meeting the source dictionary's image of the body's ribs as house-poles without requiring the terms to be identical.
Humanity is created from نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ and its mate, using nafs as the single human self from which a living population is built.
God creates people from نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ and makes its mate from it, another direct use of nafs as an originating human self.
أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ links being brought into existence with the section's claim that each human is a nafs.
At death the command أَخْرِجُوا أَنْفُسَكُمُ separates the selves from bodily life, supporting the section's living-spirit sense of nafs.
كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ gives the section's statement that every human is a nafs its universal mortal boundary.
The Lord gives each thing its خلق and then guides it, a nonlexical parallel to making a created structure fit for its mode of life.
God creates everything and فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا, stating precise determination as the order behind formed creation.
إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ generalizes measured creation, illuminating the balance and fitness carried by سَوَّاهَا.
وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدَى follows creation and proportioning in 87:2 with measure and guidance, showing what fitted completion enables.
أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا فِي الْمِيزَانِ turns the balance placed beside the raised heaven in 55:7 into a norm for human conduct.
The command to establish weight justly continues the movement from the cosmic balance of 55:7 to balanced human action.
God holds the heavens and earth from ceasing or slipping away, presenting continued preservation as part of their construction.
Seven heavens and a corresponding earth are created, with the command descending among them, making the cosmic enclosure layered and governed from within.
Earth is made ذَلُولًا so its inhabitants can walk its slopes and eat God's provision, showing the floor fitted for use rather than merely spread.
The earth is made a stable dwelling with rivers, mountains, and barriers, elaborating how the lower part of the house is secured for life.
أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ كِفَاتًا depicts earth as a containing or gathering place, an additional function of the house's lower surface.
أَحْيَاءً وَأَمْوَاتًا specifies that the earth of 77:25 gathers both living and dead occupants.
Humans are created from earth, returned to it, and brought from it again, tying the living structure materially and temporally to the floor beneath it.
God causes human beings to grow from earth like vegetation, making the third living structure arise from the house's lower member.
People are returned into earth and brought out again after the growth of 71:17, setting a boundary and renewal for the earth-born self.
God extends the shade and makes the sun its guide, developing the source section's secondary definition of an overhead expanse through the shade it casts.
God then draws the shade in gradually, showing that the canopy's shading effect is itself measured and governed.
God shades Israel with الْغَمَامَ and supplies food, showing an overhead covering functioning as merciful shelter.
The cloud again shades the people in the wilderness, a concrete instance of the section's "what rises above and shades you" definition.
وَظِلٍّ مَمْدُودٍ presents extended shade as part of the garden's prepared dwelling, a positive realization of the sheltering-canopy sense.
The command to go to a three-branched "shade" erects a false canopy whose failure to shade or protect is stated in 77:31.
The jinn find heaven filled with strong guards and flames, reporting from another speaker's stance how the protected upper boundary is experienced.
The human doubts that God will gather his bones, making bodily reconstruction explicitly a matter of joining the structure's separated parts.
God answers that He can proportion even the fingertips, joining reassembly of the bones in 75:3 to exact finishing of the smallest bodily detail.
The command to look at the bones as God raises or assembles them and then clothes them with flesh directly stages the rebuilding of the human frame.
God forms human beings in the wombs however He wills, a direct Quranic statement of the divine fashioning behind the section's third structure.
“We created you, then shaped you” makes human form the deliberate result of divine workmanship.
People standing in a compact rank are كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيَانٌ مَرْصُوصٌ; living human parts become a tightly joined building, concretizing the source definition of bināʾ as joining parts.
A building founded on reverence is set against one on a collapsing bank that falls with its builder into fire; construction becomes an exact image of the soul's moral foundation and possible ruin.
The building of 9:109 remains a source of doubt “in their hearts” until those hearts are cut, carrying the outer construction into the inward human structure.
God strikes a hostile building at its foundations so its roof falls on its occupants from above, a direct structural reversal of the protected roof over a secure floor.

During creation God addresses heaven while it is smoke and commands heaven and earth to come; their joint willing response presents roof and floor as paired participants before 41:12 completes the heavens.

The audience is told to see the heaven and earth enclosing them, then warned that earth can swallow them or a piece of heaven fall, exposing the two boundaries of the cosmic house as possible agents of collapse.
The spider's house is called the frailest of houses, giving the God-built and protected cosmic dwelling a concrete opposite in a structure unable to protect its occupant.
The objector displays decayed bones and asks who can give them life, bringing the dismantled bodily frame and loss of its living principle into one challenge.
The answer to 36:78 is that the One who originated the bones the first time will revive them, identifying their original Builder as their rebuilder.
God knows people both when He brings them from earth and when they are embryos in their mothers, directly linking the cosmic floor's material with the hidden formation of the human occupant.
The question whether people see how God created seven heavens in layers repeats the image of a deliberately built, tiered overhead structure.
God creates seven ways above the audience and is not heedless of creation, presenting the upper structure as layered and continuously attended.
The exception of a listener pursued by a visible flame shows how the guarding asserted in 15:17 actively repels an attempted breach of the adorned heaven.
The jinn explain that former listening posts at heaven are now met by a waiting flame, specifying the experienced consequence of the strong guards reported in 72:8.

The same surah's account of fashioning and breathing life into the human at 32:7-9 begins by naming God as Creator of the heavens, earth, and what lies between, reinforcing the single-Builder sequence.
Creation of the heavens and earth is joined to living creatures dispersed through them and God's power to gather them, linking the cosmic structure, its lives, and their reassembly.
The names Creator, Originator, and Fashioner identify divine forming itself as an attribute, clarifying the agent behind the section's repeated construction and proportioning verbs.
Human beings are created from dust and then spread abroad as people, making the inhabitants arise from the material of the floor on which they move.
Human formation from dust and then a drop, followed by pairing, gestation, birth, and measured lifespan, traces both the material assembly and temporal measure of the living structure.
God can replace people with their likes and produce them in a form or state they do not know, setting the present human build within His power to refashion it.
Mountains are removed and the earth is left exposed and level, dismantling the peg-and-floor arrangement used by the section's tent image.
God leaves the mountains as a level plain, turning the structural fixtures of the inhabited earth into an unfeatured final surface.
No depression or rise remains in the plain of 20:106, defining the total leveling that replaces the present fitted floor.
The earth is shaken violently, reversing the stability of the floor spread and prepared for its occupants.
The mountains are pulverized after the earth's shaking in 56:4, removing the peg-like elements along with the floor's stability.
When the mountains are set moving, the fixtures associated with holding the earthly tent cease to stand in place.
